summary: Cicero's De fato used phi0474.phi049 as canonical work and phi0474.phi056 in 96 passage-node CTS fields, although phi056 identifies Epistulae ad Familiares. Work, KG passages, corpus manifestations, translation priority and manifest now use the authoritative Perseus work phi0474.phi054; Latin edition/version exactness remains explicitly open.
resolution_criteria: Every current De fato work/passage identity remains phi0474.phi054; Latin and Yonge-English manifestations remain distinct; the Latin edition status stays open until separately adjudicated; the Cicero snapshot cohort stays at zero violations.

adjudication.decision: Normalize work identity to phi0474.phi054 without assigning an unproved Latin version identifier.
adjudication.rationale: The Perseus Catalog identifies De fato as phi054; phi056 is a different Ciceronian work. Identity correction is certain, while source-edition identity is not and must not be invented.

summary: Porphyry's Ad Marcellam work and 35 KG/corpus records used tlg2034.tlg009 as canonical identity while their source CTS correctly pointed to tlg2034.tlg005. Work, passages and corpus manifest now consistently use the authoritative OpenGreekAndLatin work tlg2034.tlg005.
resolution_criteria: Work, all 35 passage nodes, all 35 corpus rows and manifest remain aligned to tlg2034.tlg005; work-child and targeted identity tests pass.

adjudication.decision: Replace tlg2034.tlg009 with tlg2034.tlg005 throughout current Ad Marcellam records.
adjudication.rationale: The OGL First1KGreek catalog and the source CTS inventory independently identify Ad Marcellam as tlg2034.tlg005; the old parent identity contradicted its own children.
